zh8QV1.content:
OASis (Open Art Spaces in Synergy) is a European project co-funded by the European Commission
under the Creative Europe – Cooperation Medium Scale call.

OASis is composed by a network of 14 official partners and numerous associated organizations, working together to break down barriers to the art world for both artists and audiences.

The OASis project was designed to foster work with communities and to ensure that local contexts are respected and valued. In this sense, each OASis presents unique characteristics, specific to its setting, resulting in distinct approaches that are nevertheless coherent in their core purposes.

Our goal is to fosters collaboration between artists and local communities, promoting dialogue, co-creation
and cultural exchange, while providing an opportunity for artist to grow and showcase their talent through a international stage.

From 2025 to 2027, 11 organizations across 10 countries will host 13 Open Art Spaces (OAS), providing free access
to artists of all disciplines from around the world.

Each year, every partner running an OASis will welcome a minimum of 5 international artists and 3 local artists for a residency program. The project will support the residencies in every means, with a specific artist fee and with expenses covering travel, accommodation, meals, and production materials.

Each residency will result in at least one co-created artwork, developed in collaboration with the local community
and the target audiences of each partner.

Please consult the open calls to access the specific conditions of each art residency program.

zlvRk1.content:
In autumn 2025, Bethlen Square Theater will host its first art residency as part of the OASis project.
The residency will take place in the theater’s historic foyer, located in Budapest’s diverse former “Chicago” area—a neighborhood with a rich cultural past, now quieter but full of potential. The goal is to transform this space into a visible, inclusive, and vibrant meeting point for local residents, students, expats, and visitors, working closely with the local community and the theater’s team to co-create artistic, social, and spatial interventions.

For this residency, Bethlen invite artists to help reimagine the new café area as a cultural gateway—a social and intellectual hub that embodies co-creation, hospitality, and urban connection.

Bethlen is seeking 8 artists (5 international and 3 local – based in Hungary) from the following fields:

  • Visual arts / Functional design (painting, light art, street art, mixed media)

  • Performing/visual storytelling (theatre, videomaking, photography, etc.)

  • Music, songwriting, or creative writing

Requirements for International Artists

  • Fluency in English (mandatory)

  • Availability for a 15-day residency between 30/11 and 14/12 2025 (mandatory)

  • Experience in community-based or art education projects will be strongly valued

What we Offer

  • ~€1300 gross artist fee

  • Up to €200 travel contribution (only international artists)

  • Accommodation (only international artists) and meals provided

  • Shared €3000 budget for artistic and production materials

  • Technical support throughout the residency

How to Apply

Send your application to medvegyandrea@bethlenszinhaz.hu including:

  • Application form (available on the call page)

  • Statement of intent (max 2 pages), describing your motivation to participate, how you plan to work with the local community and team, your artistic project ideas and your relevant skills.

  • Portfolio/website/social links showcasing your previous work

  • Short bio or CV

  • One clear, high-quality photo with your face visible (for communication use on our website and social media)

Applications will be evaluated based on artistic merit, the feasibility and impact of the proposed co-creation strategy, and the artist’s ability to connect with and engage the local community. It is also expected to have an online open house 17/07/2025 at 17:00 (CET).
The application deadline is set at 31/07/2025 and results will be announced by 15/08/2025.

This time the setting shifts from the theatre's foyer to the Mátra Hiking Camp — a nature-based site in the Hungarian mountains, out of use for four years, waiting to be reimagined as a temporary cultural space.

The central question: how can a hiking campground become a cultural oasis, and how can an off-site residency stay meaningfully connected to a downtown theatre?

Bethlen is seeking 8 artists (5 international + 3 Hungary-based) from the following fields:

  • Visual arts / spatial practices

  • Performing arts / storytelling / media

  • Design / architecture

  • Digital / hybrid practices

Requirements

  • Fluency in English (mandatory)

  • Availability for the 15-day residency: 14–28 September 2026 (mandatory)

  • Participation in 2 online meetings: 18 August & 8 September

  • Experience in community-based work is a plus

What we offer

Fill out the application form at forms.gle/2Nr6Jp9reyzwRp16A including a statement of intent (max 4,000–6,000 characters), portfolio/website links, short bio or CV, and one clear photo with your face visible.

Applications will be evaluated based on artistic quality, contextual relevance, feasibility, and community engagement.

In 2025, one proposal will be selected to join the “Bom Dia” OASis Residency, at Cultivamos Cultura for a period of 7 to 30 days during the month of September

This call is open to international creators / artists / researchers from various fields and disciplines, as well as practitioners and experts that operate at the intersection of culture and other disciplines.

Cultivamos Cultura value projects that are inspired by local or natural materials, have a strong ecological interest and are rooted in a care for a sustainable future of an expanded and diverse community. Within the OASis project, interaction with the community and exchange with international artists are valued.

The town of São Luís and the county of Odemira has a vibrant and culturally rich community, and CC encourages residents to immerse themselves in this dynamic atmosphere. Additionally, the residency fosters collaboration between creators and the community, while also cultivating synergies between different residencies.

The residents must produce an output that will be included in the group exhibition of the OASis project in 2027. Documentation of the residency will be presented on webpages and social media of the partners and the project itself. Cultivamos Cultura expects an output to be added to its collection at the end of the residency.

This residency includes:

  • A limited budget for travel of up to €500.

  • Accommodation in a private room in a shared farmhouse in the center of São Luis, within the property of Cultivamos Cultura.

  • Access to a shared kitchen equipped for meal preparation.

  • An artist fee of €1300 gross.

  • Equitable per diem for food.*

  • Production/material expenses up to a maximum of €1600.*

  • Free access to all spaces and resources of Cultivamos Cultura.

  • Access to a workspace/studio for the duration of the residency period

  • The team of Cultivamos Cultura will provide occasional support to the project, but it is expected that the selected individual is reasonably autonomous in executing and producing all phases of the project, which will be evaluated based on their portfolio from recent years.

    *For more info check the complete call accessible by clicking on the button below.

zWrvuZ.content:
Deep Work Week on Spatial Practices - Brussels (Belgium) - Deadline 19/12/2025

City Mine(d) launches a call for contributors for a Deep Work Week on Spatial Practices, a residency that explores how urban space can be reclaimed and managed outside the logics of market speculation and state control. Across Europe, access to space—whether for working, gathering, rehearsing, organising, or simply existing—is increasingly contested. Vacant buildings, informal ateliers, community-run rooms, shared desks, and self-organised venues often represent the last frontiers where collective imagination and civic experimentation can take shape.
This residency aims to question, map, and re-imagine these practices through artistic, architectural, and research-driven approaches.

From 22 February to 1 March 2026, City Mine(d) will bring together 5 international and 3 Brussels-based artists, architects, researchers, thinkers, and practitioners to reflect on how non-market, non-state spaces can be designed, financed, governed, and accessed. Participants will work intensively throughout the week, contribute to a three-day participatory planning workshop, and share work-in-progress materials during a public event on 28 February 2026.

International contributors should have a strong interest in vacant or underused buildings—either through hands-on practice or academic research—and be able to produce within one week a mapping (geographical, conceptual, visual, sonic, narrative or digital) that addresses the themes of the residency.

A good working knowledge of French and English and full availability in Brussels from 21 to 28 February 2026 are required.

Selected international participants will receive €1200 gross artist fee, a €300 contribution to travel and accommodation, and the opportunity to work closely with Brussels-based communities, organisations, and fellow contributors.

Timeline:
– Call closes 19 December 2025
– Selected applicants notified before 12 January 2026
– Short online interview and one or two preparatory sessions for invited participants
– Residency starts 21 February 2026

How to apply:
Send your application to oasiscall@citymined.org including:
– A statement of intent (max 2 pages) outlining your motivation, your experience with re-using vacant buildings, your background in working with local communities and co-creation, and your initial ideas for an artistic output mapping these themes.
– A portfolio, website or relevant links showcasing previous work.

zNyIF2.content:
Fondazione Campania Welfare is launching the second round of OASis In the Park, following the success of our first residency cycle (San Laise Open Lab). The residency is based at Parco San Laise, a former NATO base in Bagnoli, Naples, currently undergoing a gradual process of social and cultural regeneration.
The OASis operates as a diffused platform across multiple spaces within the park, combining artistic creation, community engagement, and social activation. OASis in the Park will take place between September and October 2026, with each selected artist staying for approximately two weeks within that period.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We welcome artists interested in developing participatory, socially engaged practices with strong educational and/or community-focused components. While we particularly encourage applications from artists interested in working with children, youth, and local communities, we welcome submissions from artists working on projects of broader social relevance to the Bagnoli area and wider community regeneration.
The residency will focus on a wide range of artistic fields, including:

  • Filmmaking and audiovisual media

  • Photography

  • Visual arts (sculpture, street art, graffiti, painting)

  • Textile, fashion and material practices

  • Music and sound

  • AI-based artistic production

  • Spatial design and installation art

  • Lighting design and light-based practices

  • Interior and community-oriented design

  • Illustration and graphic arts

Artists from any other discipline are equally welcome. We value multidisciplinarity and are open to any practice that can generate real impact within the community.

RESIDENCY ACTIVITIES

We expect applicants to propose concrete ideas for their time at the OASis. Activities may include workshops, co-creation sessions, personal artistic but community-based projects, training initiatives, or other artistic interventions — but you have full creative freedom. What matters is generating meaningful engagement and producing specific outputs relevant to the local context.
The specific focus of each residency will be discussed and refined during the selection phase.

HOW TO APPLY and WHAT WE OFFER

Send your application to fcw.oasis@gmail.com with subject line "OASis In the Park Application", including:

  1. CV (max 2 pages)

  2. Portfolio (links, images, or documentation of previous work)

  3. Artistic Project Proposal (max 2 pages) — describe your proposed project, how you intend to engage with the local community, and the outputs you aim to produce. Proposals will be discussed during the selection phase and there is room for flexibility and adaptation.

  4. Artist fee: €1,300

  5. Travel, meals, accommodation, and production costs: fully covered by the project

SELECTION CRITERIA AND TIMELINE

  • Artistic quality and originality

  • Capacity for participatory and socially engaged practice

  • Relevance to local context and community needs

  • Clarity and concreteness of the proposed project

  • Call closes: 26 June 2026

  • Artists notified: July 2026

  • Residency period: September – October 2026

Aligned with the objectives of the project, we will select 5 international (EU citizens or residents in EU) and 3 local (Campania Region) artists.

Results will be announced by 18 July 2026. Given the volume of applications we typically receive, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted directly. If you have not heard from us by mid-July, please consider your application unsuccessful for this round.

zUshnC.content:
What stories do cemeteries whisper to the city?
Can we uncover their hidden layers of architecture, identity, and exclusion? What should the intercultural cemeteries of European metropolises look like?

This summer, the Other Space Foundation invites 4 international contributors to join a unique 7–10 day interdisciplinary art residency in the heart of Poland’s capital. Together, we will explore the overlooked urban ecologies of cemeteries – as spaces of memory, invisibility, and cultural intersection.

Inspired by the concept of “Shadow Architecture” (series of books and interdisciplinary activities around them) developed by Polish architect and artist Aleksandra Wasilkowska, this edition invites artists to delve into the margins of official urban narratives. Cemeteries – often hidden in plain sight – represent both architectural absence and deep cultural presence. They raise questions about belonging, sacredness, public space, and how we remember.

We are looking for proposals that:

  • Engage with cemeteries as architectural, social, or symbolic spaces

  • Explore the topic of death, passing, rituals, mourning

  • Use artistic strategies to illuminate stories of exclusion, care, or remembrance

  • Explore interdisciplinary forms: visual art, performance, storytelling, sound, design

  • Are rooted in community-based, site-specific or research-driven practices

The Other Space Foundation is inviting:

  • 4 international contributors - photographers, architects, researchers, artists who will work with local contributors

Requirements for international artists:

  • Interest and experience (expertise and/or practical) in the subject of the call,

  • Fluency in English

  • Availability between 13 and 30 August 2025 in Warsaw

  • Experience in socially engaged or community-based art is a strong asset


What we offer for international artists

  • €1300 gross artist fee

  • Travel budget up to €200

  • Accommodation in Warsaw-based OASis - renowned Teatr Powszechny and stay allowances

  • Networking with local communities, researchers and other contributors,

  • Agreed budget on production

Fill this form to apply.

zjrWGn.content:
The Other Space Foundation, together with Warszawski Klub Wodniaków PTTK and The Academic Association of FoA WUT, invites artists, architects, designers, researchers, filmmakers, video artists, performers, musicians, community animators and other interdisciplinary contributors to join OASis Warsaw 2026.

This year's Warsaw edition takes place across two OASes and two residency periods. Applicants may express interest in one or both contexts; the final selection will assign each selected contributor to one residency only.

OASis #1 – Warszawski Klub Wodniaków PTTK - 26 July – 3 August 2026

Can a harbour become an even more vibrant cultural, social and community space?

The first Warsaw OASis Residency takes place at Warszawski Klub Wodniaków PTTK, a long-standing community harbour on the banks of the Vistula River — for decades a gathering point for boaters, kayakers and local residents.
This residency explores how artistic, architectural, educational and community-based activities can strengthen this unique place while respecting its traditions. Selected activities may also extend to other urban water spaces in Warsaw — riverbanks, waterways, canals and floating locations.

We are looking for contributors working in participatory architecture, spatial interventions, placemaking, music and performance, video art, filmmaking, visual and public art, community animation, and interdisciplinary practices connecting art, ecology, education or active recreation. We especially value proposals involving direct collaboration with harbour users and local communities.

Selected contributors: 5 (3 international, 2 Warsaw-based)

OASis #2 – Open Studio Jazdów - 18 September – 2 October 2026

"For me the most important thing is to find a place where I could play an active role in a community... Unfortunately it's very expensive and has many regulations, so it's almost undoable." — Is it?

Jazdów OASis is based at Wolny Jazdów — an independent community of Finnish wooden houses built in 1945, just 300 metres from the Polish Parliament. Home to dozens of NGOs and informal groups, it is a rare open, non-profit space in one of Poland's most commercialised cities, increasingly under pressure from gentrification.

We invite socially engaged artists to explore what it means to protect and activate places like this. We welcome proposals across architecture, spatial design, installation, filmmaking, visual arts, and any other discipline capable of generating real impact — particularly with children, youth and local communities. Applicants should come with concrete ideas: workshops, co-creation sessions, community-based projects or other interventions, with full creative freedom on approach.

Selected contributors: 2 (1 international, 1 Warsaw-based)

What We Offer
€1,300 gross contributor fee · Travel support up to €200 · Accommodation and boarding · Production budget · Working and presentation space · Access to local communities and networks

Selection Criteria
Artistic quality · Capacity for participatory practice · Relevance to local context · Openness to collaboration · Feasibility

Deadline: 4 July 2026, 23:59 CET — Results published around 8 July.

zDN59g.content:
Set within one of Lisbon’s most distinctive cultural venues, the residency invites authors, creators, artists, and researchers from different fields to develop site-specific work in dialogue with the spaces, atmosphere, and daily life of the Goethe-Institut. Housed in the remarkable Valmor Palace, the institute offers a layered environment where historical architecture, cultural activity, and public use intersect, creating a strong setting for artistic experimentation and public engagement.

Applicants are invited to propose an intervention for one of three designated areas within the Goethe-Institut building:

Intervention Areas
● Glass in the cafeteria – a highly visible area in one of the most frequented parts of the building, where people gather throughout the day to eat, study, work, and spend time. It is also located near the entrance to the Auditorium.
● Wall on the staircase leading to the cafeteria – a prominent wall in a transition area used daily by visitors moving between different parts of the Valmor Palace, including the cafeteria, the Library, and the outdoor garden.
● Garden wall and fence – an outdoor intervention area located in the garden of the Valmor Palace, surrounding one of the terrace spaces and remaining visible both to those using the area and to people passing through it.

The residency programme is structured around three main phases:

Programme Phases
● Initial design and production phase – after selection, artists will be given a defined period to further develop their concept and begin production. During this phase, follow-up meetings will be held with Gerador.
● Artistic residency – the residency will last 7 working days and will support the final development of the selected works. The residency should include interaction with the local community and will culminate in the presentation of an output as part of the Artistic Journey Showcase.
● Exhibition – from 6 October to 1 November 2026, the works developed during the residency will be presented in a collective exhibition at the Goethe-Institut in Lisbon, alongside five works created by local artists.

Who Can Apply
The call is open to authors, creators, artists, and researchers from different disciplines. Eligible applicants include non-Portuguese nationals living in Portugal, as well as residents of other European Union countries or other countries covered by the Creative Europe Programme.

Important Dates
● Applications open on 10 April 2026 and close on 24 May 2026, at 20:00 GMT.
● Shortlisted candidates will be notified by 5 June 2026, with online interviews taking place until 26 June 2026.
● Selected artists will be announced on 30 June 2026.
● The artistic residencies will take place over 7 working days between 31 August and 25 September 2026.
● The final exhibition will run from 6 October to 1 November 2026.

Support Package
● Author fee: EUR 1,300 gross, taxes included.
● Materials and production budget: up to EUR 400, subject to prior approval by Gerador.
● Accommodation in Lisbon during the residency period.
● Meals provided by Gerador during the residency.
● Workspace: a 25 m² room available for use during the residency period.

Artistic Intelligence – Nature and Technology - Maribor (Slovenia) - Deadline 26/09/2025

Deadline to apply: 26 September 2025

Association for Culture and Education KIBLA (ACE KIBLA) is launching its first OASis Residency in Maribor, Slovenia, in autumn 2025, inviting 4 international artists, researchers, and interdisciplinary practitioners.

The residency will explore the intersection of nature, technology, and cultural/natural heritage in the Maribor region, engaging with themes such as ecology, energy, history, and the future. Artists are encouraged to work across analog and digital media – including AR, VR, XR, AI, visual arts, performance, music, literature, and community-based practices.

Residencies will take place at KIBLA PORTAL (a former textile factory turned cultural hub) and KIBLA2LAB, equipped with advanced XR, 3D scanning, and photogrammetry technologies. Participants will be encouraged to combine research, production, and artistic experimentation, involving the local community through interactive, participatory approaches.

Residency Dates

Applicants must be based in EU Member States or Creative Europe eligible countries.

  • 2–11 November 2025

  • 12–21 November 2025

What We Offer

  • €1300 gross artist fee

  • Travel support up to €300

  • Accommodation in Maribor (private or shared)

  • Studio and workspace access

  • Curatorial and production support

  • Materials support (to be agreed in advance)

Eligibility & Proposals

We welcome proposals that:

  • Address Maribor’s people, history, and social context

  • Show strong artistic originality and quality

  • Are research-driven within art and media culture

  • Engage with the local community

How to Apply

Send applications to kibla@kibla.org by 26 September 2025, including:

  • CV or detailed bio

  • Portfolio or website link

  • Artistic proposal (max 300 words or 10-slide PDF) outlining: motivation, community engagement strategy, concept, materials, methods, and production needs

  • (Optional) short video/audio (max 3 minutes)

  • One clear photo (for communication purposes)

Selection & Results

Applications will be evaluated on artistic quality, originality, feasibility, and co-creation strategies.
Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an online interview.
Final results will be announced by 10 October 2025.

📩 For questions write to kibla@kibla.org or visit the website.

zjqv7L.content:
Machaon International, together with Kolaj 22 and the Ukrainian-Slovak HUB, invites artists to participate in Disappearing Landscape — an artistic residency set in the High Tatras and the wider Carpathian region of Slovakia. The residency brings together international and local artists, youth culture, and independent creative spaces to respond to the accelerating loss of natural habitats, wildlife corridors, and authentic mountain life through artistic practice, community engagement, and cultural activism.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking artists interested in developing projects that engage with environmental change, disappearing landscapes, and the relationship between culture, environment, community, and activism. We welcome visual artists, photographers, filmmakers, musicians, sound artists, performers, sculptors, and interdisciplinary creators. Artists working in any other discipline are equally welcome — we value multidisciplinarity and are open to any practice capable of generating meaningful dialogue between art, ecology, and community.

RESIDENCY FOCUS

The High Tatras and surrounding Carpathian landscapes face mounting pressure from uncontrolled construction, tourism expansion, and habitat fragmentation — forest ecosystems, wildlife corridors, and authentic mountain life are rapidly disappearing.
Projects should engage with these dynamics, whether through landscape degradation, environmental activism, youth culture, or regeneration and community rebuilding.
The residency also welcomes projects connected to the story of Kolaj 22, an independent cultural space in Poprad destroyed by fire in 2025, and the broader themes of resilience and cultural rebuilding it embodies. Artists have full creative freedom in how they structure their work, provided the project produces a publicly presentable output and engages meaningfully with local communities.

WHAT WE OFFER

Selected artists receive an artist fee of €1,300 (maximum per project, individual or collective; taxes at artist's charge), travel support of up to €300, and production/material support of up to €300. Accommodation and meals are provided by the organisers, together with access to workspaces, partner venues, and excursions in the High Tatras region.

HOW TO APPLY

Send your application in English in PDF format to zapovedniks@gmail.com, subject line: DISAPPEARING LANDSCAPE 2026 – Application – Your Name, including:

  • Project Proposal (max. 700 words)

  • Portfolio or website links

  • CV (max. 2 pages)

  • Five images of the project

  • Brief overview of technical needs and timeline

Proposals will be discussed during the selection phase with room for flexibility and adaptation

  • Application deadline: 22 June 2026

  • Artists notified: July 2026

  • Residency: 14–22 August 2026

zdGaJT.content:
Wild Nature – TAI - Talin (Armenia) - Deadline 17/08/2025

🔍 Residency Concept

What happens when a landscape loses its colours? Talin, once rich in wildflowers, herbs, and traditional ecological knowledge, is now witnessing the quiet disappearance of these species, mirroring a broader erosion of cultural memory. Plants that were once central to healing, dyeing, food, and ritual are now endangered. Today, climate change, soil degradation, rural depopulation, and the decline of traditional crafts threaten both the plants and the knowledge they carry.
This residency invites participants to explore these vanishing elements through sensory engagement including textiles, sound, visual art (bio art, eco art, food based practices, street art, painting, installation, textile art, sculpture, and mixed media) and collaborative practices. In partnership with local communities, artists will reanimate these stories and reimagine new ways of preserving ecological and cultural memory.

Two possible residency periods: 10–20 September 2025 or 22 September – 1 October 2025

📍 About the Location – Talin, Aragatsotn

Located at the foot of Mount Aragats, about 63 km from Yerevan, Talin is a historic town with deep-rooted traditions and ecological richness. Its landscapes ranging from steppe grasslands to volcanic soils, host endemic and culturally significant plants now at risk. The town is known for its 7th-century cathedral and a strong sense of rural resilience, making it an ideal place for artists interested in site-specific and community-based practice.

TAI is Looking For Proposals That:

  • Address ecology and disappearing flora of Aragatsotn

  • Co-creation through community engagement or participatory practices

  • Are site-specific or research-driven, rooted in local context

  • Strong artistic quality and clear relevance to the theme

💼 What We Offer

  • €1300 gross artist fee

  • Travel budget up to €300

  • Accommodation in Talin (private or shared)

  • Access to studio / workspace; curatorial support throughout the residency; materials and production support

Today Art Initiative launches the second edition of OASis, establishing a new creative and community-centered space in Yerevan following the first residency in Talin. OASis operates as a multidisciplinary platform across multiple spaces within the park, combining artistic creation, community engagement, education, and social activation.

This edition focuses on air pollution and air as a shared environmental condition — we invite artistic approaches engaging with air as material, atmosphere, or invisible presence. Final artworks will contribute to public discussions on environmental awareness and urban ecology.

We are looking for artists across a wide range of disciplines, including:

  • New media art

  • Installation art

  • Sound art

  • Bio art

  • Textile and material practices

  • Visual arts

Artists from any other discipline are equally welcome — we value multidisciplinarity and openness to practices capable of generating meaningful community impact.

Residency activities may include workshops, co-creation sessions, community-based projects, and public interventions. Applicants are encouraged to propose concrete ideas, with creative freedom to develop them further during the selection process.

What we offer

  • Artist fee of up to €1,300 (gross)

  • Free accommodation

  • Travel support up to €315

  • Full production support and coverage of production costs

Open to artists legally residing in Creative Europe participating countries. Collective applications are welcome — financial conditions are provided per selected project, not per participant.

How to apply

Send your application to todayartinitiative@gmail.com, subject line "OASis in Yerevan," including: CV (max 2 pages), portfolio, and project proposal (max 2 pages) describing your project, community engagement approach, and intended outputs. Indicate your preferred session(s).

Timeline

  • Deadline: 7 July 2026

  • Notification: by 13 July 2026

  • Session 1: 12–27 August 2026

  • Session 2: 28 August – 12 September 2026

Final artworks will be presented at the NEXA 1st Contemporary Art Festival in Yerevan.

ccBodyTxt2.content:
For 2027, one proposal will be selected to join the “Bom Dia” OASis Residency at Cultivamos Cultura, for a period of 7 to 30 days during the month of March.

The call is open to international creators, artists and researchers from any field, and to practitioners working at the intersection of culture and other disciplines. Applications may be individual or by a group of no more than two people — conditions and funding are the same either way — and the selected resident must be present at Cultivamos Cultura for the whole approved period.

The residency sits within the OASis programme, so it opens onto the local community through artist talks, walks, workshops or open studio visits. São Luís and the wider county of Odemira hold a vibrant and culturally rich community.

Each residency produces an artistic output, which joins the OASis group exhibition in 2027 and is presented both to the local public and across the OASis network. One output is added to the Cultivamos Cultura collection.

This residency includes:

  • A travel budget of up to €500.

  • Accommodation in a private room in a shared farmhouse in the centre of São Luís, within the Cultivamos Cultura property.

  • Access to a shared kitchen equipped for preparing meals.

  • A project grant of €1.300.

  • An equitable daily food allowance.

  • Production and material costs up to €1.600.

  • Free access to every Cultivamos Cultura space and resource, and to a studio for the whole period.

Important. Production and material funding is limited and must be approved by Cultivamos Cultura before anything is bought. The amount is transferred on invoice, which must carry the tax number (NIF) and the details of Cultivamos Cultura.

Deadlines and application

The call runs until 30 October 2026, 18:00 CET, or until 100 applications have been received — whichever comes first. Proposals submitted later are not considered. Results are announced in the third week of December, by email and through the Cultivamos Cultura and OASis channels.

Projects inspired by local or natural materials are valued, as is a strong ecological interest and a care for the sustainable future of a diverse community. Within OASis, interaction with the local community and exchange with international artists carry particular weight. One thing to weigh before applying: inside São Luís the community speaks mostly Portuguese, and reaching beyond the village means renting a car out of the production grant.

Proposals must include:

  • A project description or statement of intent (max. 500 words) with images, drawings or diagrams, setting out your vision and how you would engage the community.

  • An estimated list of resources and materials.

  • A signed declaration of originality.

  • Your portfolio or website, and a short CV (max. 4 pages).

  • A timeline for implementing the project.

  • Five photographs, drawings or illustrative images of the project, for communication purposes should you be selected.

Artistic Intelligence – Nature and Technology - Maribor (Slovenia) - Deadline 19/10/2026

Association for Culture and Education KIBLA (ACE KIBLA) opens its second OASis Residency in Maribor, Slovenia, and invites 2 international artists, researchers and interdisciplinary practitioners to take part in autumn 2026.

The call is open to practitioners working across analog and digital media — audio and visual culture, fine art, performance, literature and theory — and to those whose work involves community practice. The residency looks at where nature and technology meet: augmented, virtual and mixed realities, artificial intelligence, and the cultural and natural heritage of the Maribor region, read through ecology, energy and the passage from its history to its future.

Work can move from analog to digital and back. Sound and vision, interactivity, audience participation and collaborative practice are all welcome, and artists are encouraged to keep their own poetics while letting the place, its people and its environment shape the outcome.

We are looking for proposals that:

  • Speak to the city, its people and its society.

  • Are artistically original and grounded in the local context.

  • Can be research-driven within art and media culture.

  • Carry a strong artistic quality and a voice of their own.

Residency period: 19–27 November 2026. Applicants must reside in an EU Member State or in a country eligible under the Creative Europe programme.

What we offer:

  • An artist fee of €1.300 gross.

  • A travel budget of up to €300.

  • Accommodation in Maribor, in a private or shared room.

  • Access to studio and workspaces.

  • Curatorial support throughout the residency.

  • Materials and production support, agreed in advance.

How to apply. Send your materials to kibla@kibla.org by 19 October 2026.

Your application must include:

  • A CV or detailed bio, as a link or a PDF of no more than 10 MB.

  • A portfolio or website.

  • An artistic proposal — max. 300 words, or a PDF of up to 10 slides — covering your motivation, how you would engage the local community, your concept, materials and methods, and any production needs.

  • Optionally, a short video or audio piece of no more than three minutes.

  • One clear photograph with a visible face, for communication purposes.
